bach.!-.name: bach.!-
bach.!-.description:
Performs subtractions between lllls or
		between lllls and numbers, with reversed inlets:
		Left operand goes in right inlet and right operand goes in left inlet.

outlets.digest: The (reverse) subtraction of the two operands

bach.!/.name: bach.!/
bach.!/.description:
Performs divisions between lllls or
		between lllls and numbers, with reversed inlets:
		Left operand goes in right inlet and right operand goes in left inlet.

outlets.digest: The (reverse) division of the two operands

bach.<.name: bach.<
bach.<.digest: Compare two lllls for less than condition
bach.<.description: Compares two lllls for less than condition, in numerical/lexicographical order.

bach.<=.name: bach.<=
bach.<=.digest: Compare two lllls for less than or equal condition
bach.<=.description: Compares two lllls for less than or equal condition, in numerical/lexicographical order.

bach.>.name: bach.>
bach.>.digest: Compare two lllls for greater than condition
bach.>.description: Compares two lllls for greater than condition, in numerical/lexicographical order.

bach.>=.name: bach.>=
bach.>=.digest: Compare two lllls for greater than or equal condition
bach.>=.description: Compares two lllls for greater than or equal condition, in numerical/lexicographical order.

bach.adj.name: bach.adj
bach.adj.digest: Compute the adjugate of a matrix
bach.adj.description:
Computes the adjugate (or the classical adjoint) of an incoming matrix,
		i.e. the transposed of the matrix whose entries are the cofactors of the incoming matrix.
		If such a matrix can't be computed (for instance for non-wellshaped or non-square matrices)
		a bang is output through the right outlet.

outlets.digest: A bang is output if no adjugate matrix could be computed.

bach.approx.name: bach.approx
bach.approx.digest: Snap pitches or MIDIcents to microtonal grid
bach.approx.description:
Approximates the incoming llll containing pitches or MIDIcents
		with the nearest pitches or MIDIcents in a specific microtonal grid.

inlets.digest: The llll containing original pitches or MIDIcents

outlets.digest: The llll containing snapped pitches or MIDIcents

bach.args.name: bach.args
bach.args.description:
Parses and retrieves the subpatcher's "normal" and attribute-style arguments.
		bach.args should be used in every subpatch or abstraction accepting arguments,
		and all the patcher's inlets should be connected to it.

inlets.digest: Bang to output all the arguments

outlets.digest: Bang after all the stored lllls have been output

bach.autoscale.name: bach.autoscale
bach.autoscale.description:
Linearly rescales all the numbers in an llll so that the minimum
		and the maximum be two given numbers.

bach.bachtree2omtree.name: bach.bachtree2omtree
bach.bachtree2omtree.digest: Convert a bach rhythmic tree into an OpenMusic rhythmic tree
bach.bachtree2omtree.description:
Converts a the measureinfo and the duration rhythmic tree (in bach form, as outputted by bach.score)
		into an OpenMusic-formatted rhythmic tree.

inlets.digest: The bach Durations tree (as symbolic rational values)

bach.beatbox.name: bach.beatbox
bach.beatbox.digest: Box voice-wise parameters into measure-wise information
bach.beatbox.description:
Adds a parenthesis level representing measures in a plain list of parameters.
		More precisely, it formats plain lists of bach.score parameters into measure-wise packets,
		according to the given time signature(s).

bach.beatunbox.name: bach.beatunbox
bach.beatunbox.digest: Flatten measure-wise parameters into plain voice-wise information
bach.beatunbox.description:
Removes the measure parenthesis levels in the bach.score parameters syntax.
		More specifically, it converts the measure-wise score syntax into a plain sequence of separate parameters
		(boxed only voice-wise, and no longer measure-wise).

inlets.digest: Whole bach.score gathered syntax, or Measureinfo (in

outlets.digest: Measureinfo – in "separate" mode: Pitches or MIDIcents
Pitches or MIDIcents – in "separate" mode: Durations
Extras (only existing when the mode is NOT "separate")

bach.belong.name: bach.belong
bach.belong.digest: Tell if some elements belong to a llll
bach.belong.description:
Tells if one or more elements belong to a given llll.
		The condition for which an element belongs to the llll can be customized via
		a lambda loop.

inlets.digest: The llll possibly containing the elements

outlets.digest: 1 if all elements belong to the llll container, 0 otherwise

bach.bin.name: bach.bin
bach.bin.description:
Computes the binomial coefficient (N K) = N! / (K! * (N-K)!),
		corresponding to the number K-element subsets in a set containing N elements.

inlets.digest: The number N, or the list N K

bach.bitdecode.name: bach.bitdecode
bach.bitdecode.description: Tells which bits are on in a given integer.

inlets.digest: The number whose bits must be decoded

bach.cartesianprod.name: bach.cartesianprod
bach.cartesianprod.description: bach.cartesianprod returns the cartesian product of two or more lllls.

bach.cartopol.name: bach.cartopol
bach.cartopol.digest: Cartesian to polar coordinate conversion for lllls
bach.cartopol.description:
Converts two lllls consisting of real and imaginary values into
		two polar-coordinate lllls consisting of amplitudes (radius) and angle values (in radians).

inlets.digest: The real parts or X coordinates
The imaginary parts or Y coordinates

bach.change.name: bach.change
bach.change.digest: Filter out repetitions of an llll
bach.change.description:
The purpose of bach.change is the to act like a change object for lllls,
		outputting the incoming llll only if it differs from the one previously entered.

inlets.digest: The llll to be possibly filtered
Set incoming llll without triggering output

outlets.digest: The incoming llll if it changed
bang if the incoming llll hasn't changed

bach.chordrev.name: bach.chordrev
bach.chordrev.digest: Reverse the non-rest elements of an llll
bach.chordrev.description:
Accepts an llll to reverse, an llll of reference durations,
		and reverses only the elements of the left llll corresponding to non-negative elements in the
		durations llll.

bach.chordrot.name: bach.chordrot
bach.chordrot.digest: Rotate the non-rest elements of an llll
bach.chordrot.description:
Accepts an llll to rotate, an llll of reference durations,
		and rotates only the elements of the left llll corresponding to non-negative elements in the
		durations llll.

bach.circle.name: bach.circle
bach.circle.description:
The purpose of bach.circle is to act as a simple clock diagram,
		where each point can represent any abstract concept as pitch-classes
		or rhythmic positions on a looped grid.
		Each point may have a velocity also. Some of the points can be selected, thus representing
		for instance pitch-class sets ("chords" or "scales"...) or rhythmic patterns.

inlets.digest: Points, or a 2-depth list of interlaced Points and Velocities

outlets.digest: Points, as a plain list of point indices
bang when changed via the interface

bach.clip.name: bach.clip
bach.clip.digest: Limit elements of lllls within a certain range
bach.clip.description:
Constraints each element of the incoming llll
		into a given numerical range, defined by a lower and
		an upper boundary.

bach.comb.name: bach.comb
bach.comb.description: Returns the combinations of the elements of a given llll.

bach.combinevoices.name: bach.combinevoices
bach.combinevoices.digest: Combine voices into a new bach.roll or bach.score
bach.combinevoices.description:
Takes in input a list of bach.roll's or bach.score's gathered syntaxes and
		combines them to make a new object listing all the input voices.

inlets.digest: List of bach.score's or bach.roll's gathered syntaxes

outlets.digest: The gathered syntax of the combined bach.roll or bach.score

bach.compl.name: bach.compl
bach.compl.digest: Find complement of a pitch-class set
bach.compl.description:
Given a pitch-class set, bach.compl
		finds its complement, i.e. the set of all the numbers not appearing in the given set.

inlets.digest: Pitch-class set (as a plain list) or tree of pitch-clas sets.

bach.constraints.name: bach.constraints
bach.constraints.description:
Solves constraints satisfaction problems.
		The rules for the evaluation of each constraint must be provided in the object's lambda loop, each associated to a unique arbitrary name.

bach.convertbase.name: bach.convertbase
bach.convertbase.description: Converts numbers from any base to any other base.

inlets.digest: The number in the original base
The digits in the original base

outlets.digest: The number in the target base
The digits in the target base

bach.coprime.name: bach.coprime
bach.coprime.description:
Tells if the incoming number are coprime,
		i.e. if their greatest common divisor is 1.

bach.coprimeser.name: bach.coprimeser
bach.coprimeser.description:
Finds all the numbers M smaller than the absolute value of a given number N
		such that M and N are coprime.

bach.counter.name: bach.counter
bach.counter.description:
The role of bach.counter is to act as a multi-indexed version of counter,
		storing in its internal memory not only a single increasing
		or decreasing index, but a list of indices, each of which can independently
		increase or decrease.

inlets.digest: bang, integer, list or llll to increment or decrement

arguments.name: options
arguments.digest: Function depends on number of arguments

bach.cross.name: bach.cross
bach.cross.digest: Compute the cross product of two lllls
bach.cross.description: Computes the cross product (or vector product) of two lllls having 3 coordinates.

bach.defer.name: bach.defer
bach.defer.digest: Put an llll at the front of the low-priority queue
bach.defer.description: Puts the incoming llll at the front of the low-priority queue.

bach.deferlow.name: bach.deferlow
bach.deferlow.digest: Put an llll at the tail of the low-priority queue
bach.deferlow.description: Puts the incoming llll at the tail of the low-priority queue.

bach.delace.name: bach.delace
bach.delace.description: Redistributes elements of an llll into several output lllls, in a round-robin fashion.

arguments.name: parameters
arguments.digest: number of outlets / mono mode and number of sublists

bach.derive.name: bach.derive
bach.derive.description: Computes the derivative of a breakpoint function or of a general function defined via a lambda loop.

inlets.digest: Breakpoint function llll or sampling parameters

bach.det.name: bach.det
bach.det.digest: Compute the determinant of a matrix
bach.det.description:
Computes the determinant of the incoming matrix. 
		For non-square matrices, the product of the pivots is output.

outlets.digest: The determinant of the incoming matrix

bach.diag.name: bach.diag
bach.diag.description: Builds a diagonal matrix having the incoming llll as diagonal.

inlets.digest: The llll to be put on the diagonal

outlets.digest: The matrix having the input llll as diagonal

bach.dict2llll.name: bach.dict2llll
bach.dict2llll.digest: Convert a dictionary into an llll
bach.dict2llll.description: Converts a dictionary into an llll, under the convention that the first element in each level is the level key.

bach.diff.name: bach.diff
bach.diff.description: Returns the difference of two lllls.

bach.divisors.name: bach.divisors
bach.divisors.description: Returns all the divisors of an integer number, in ascending order.

bach.dl2curve.name: bach.dl2curve
bach.dl2curve.digest: Convert a duration line into pitch and velocity curve~ messages
bach.dl2curve.description:
Converts the information about the duration line of a note
		into messages to drive a pitch curve~ and a velocity curve~.

outlets.digest: Messages for the curve~ controlling the pitch
Messages for the curve~ controlling the velocity

bach.dl2line.name: bach.dl2line
bach.dl2line.digest: Convert a duration line into pitch and velocity line~ messages
bach.dl2line.description:
Converts the information about the duration line of a note
		into messages to drive a pitch line~ and a velocity line~.
		The slopes of the duration line segments are ignored.

outlets.digest: Messages for the line~ controlling the pitch
Messages for the line~ controlling the velocity

bach.drip.name: bach.drip
bach.drip.digest: Automatically step through lllls with delays
bach.drip.description:
The purpose of bach.drip is to automatically output elements of an llll,
		with a given delay between each couple of output elements.

inlets.digest: The llll to be stepped through

outlets.digest: A bang when dripping is completed

bach.dsort.name: bach.dsort
bach.dsort.description:
Sorts a list depending to the distance of its
		element to a given fixed number (nearest elements coming first, farthest element at the end).

bach.dx2x.name: bach.dx2x
bach.dx2x.description:
Constructs an llll starting from a given number
		and then summing one by one the numeric steps
		contained in the incoming differences llll.

bach.eig.name: bach.eig
bach.eig.description: Finds the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the incoming matrix, via the power iteration method.

inlets.digest: The eigenvectors relative to the eigenvalues, listed by rows

bach.enharm.name: bach.enharm
bach.enharm.description:
Modifies the enharmonicity of the incoming pitches, either by adding diatonic
		steps, or via automatic respelling

inlets.digest: Difference in diatonic steps, or "auto" symbol
llll with values or new expression

bach.extractbasis.name: bach.extractbasis
bach.extractbasis.description:
Extracts a set of linearly independent vectors from an incoming list of vectors.
		Depending on its attributes, it can also transform the vectors so that they be orthogonal and/or unitary.

outlets.digest: The extracted set of independent vectors

bach.ezmidiplay.name: bach.ezmidiplay
bach.ezmidiplay.description:
Converts the data coming from the playout of bach.roll or
		bach.score into a MIDI stream, and plays it.

bach.fact.name: bach.fact
bach.fact.description:
Computes the factorial of a given number N, that is
		N! = N*(N-1)*(N-2)...*2*1.

outlets.digest: The factorial of the number N

bach.factorize.name: bach.factorize
bach.factorize.description: Returns the factorization of an integer.

bach.fft.name: bach.fft
bach.fft.description:
Performs the Fast Fourier transform on
		the incoming llll (whatever its size is), and outputs
		either the cartesian or the polar representation.

outlets.digest: Output phases (in radiants) or imaginary (y) parts

bach.filternull.name: bach.filternull
bach.filternull.description:
Takes the incoming data and
		outputs it through its first outlet only if it is
		not a null llll; otherwise it sends a bang
		or a default llll through the second outlet.

outlets.digest: bang or default if incoming llll is null

bach.float2rat.name: bach.float2rat
bach.float2rat.digest: Approximate a floating point number with a rational number
bach.float2rat.description:
Approximates a floating point number with a rational number, within
		a given error threshold and with a given maximum denominator.

bach.fromc&r.name: bach.fromc&r
bach.fromc&r.description:
Accepts an llll of element corresponding to chords,
		an llll of elements corresponding to rests, and an llll corresponding to the
		position of rests, and interlaces the two lists properly. This is typically
		used in combination with bach.toc&r.

inlets.digest: The llll of elements corresponding to non-rests
The llll of elements corresponding to rests
The original indices of the rest elements

bach.funnel.name: bach.funnel
bach.funnel.description:
Index each llll element by prepending an increasing integer to it, and wrapping them
		in a pair of parentheses.

bach.gausselim.name: bach.gausselim
bach.gausselim.description:
Applies the Gaussian elimination algorithm to reduce the incoming matrix to a row echelon form.
		It also outputs some additional information, such as determinant and rank.

outlets.digest: The number of line swaps that have been performed
The rank of the original matrix
the determinant of the original matrix

bach.gcd.name: bach.gcd
bach.gcd.description: Computes the greatest common divisor of two numbers or of an llll.

inlets.digest: The first number or the llll of numbers

outlets.digest: The greatest common divisor of the numbers

bach.getcol.name: bach.getcol
bach.getcol.digest: Get a column of a matrix
bach.getcol.description: Extracts a column of a matrix in llll form.

bach.getrow.name: bach.getrow
bach.getrow.digest: Get a row of a matrix
bach.getrow.description: Extracts a row of a matrix in llll form.

bach.graph.name: bach.graph
bach.graph.description:
The purpose of bach.graph is to act as a simple graph plotter: once the expression
		of the curve to draw has been set (in the first inlet) possibly along with its parameters
		(in the second inlet), a bang will plot the curve. Vector representation are also possible.

inlets.digest: Set formulas or bang to plot graph
All the parameters of the inserted formulas

outlets.digest: Dumped interleaved list of X Y couples
bang when user changes the graph with the mouse

bach.histo.name: bach.histo
bach.histo.description: Builds an histogram starting from a list of data, returning elements along with their occurrences.

inlets.digest: The minimum integer value to be accounted for (or "auto")
The maximum integer value to be accounted for (or "auto")

arguments.name: minimum
arguments.digest: The minimum integer value to be accounted for (or "auto")

arguments.name: maximum
arguments.digest: The maximum integer value to be accounted for (or "auto")

bach.hypercomment.name: bach.hypercomment
bach.hypercomment.description:
Works like a standard comment object, with the possibility to easily have
		hyperlink references inside it.

bach.idmatrix.name: bach.idmatrix
bach.idmatrix.description: Builds the identity square matrix of a given size.

bach.idvector.name: bach.idvector
bach.idvector.description: Builds versors having all 0's as entries, except for a 1 in a given position (or combinations of such versors).

bach.ifunc.name: bach.ifunc
bach.ifunc.digest: Compute interval function of two pitch-class sets
bach.ifunc.description:
Reports the interval function of two pitch-class sets. The interval function between
		two sets A and B is defined as ifunc(A, B)_k = #{(x, y), x in A, y in B such that x-y = k}, roughly
		equivalent to saying that it is a vector where the k entry tells how many intervals of k steps
		can be formed by taking the first note from set A and the second note from set B.

bach.im.name: bach.im
bach.im.digest: Find the image of a matrix
bach.im.description: Finds the image of an incoming matrix A, i.e. its column span.

bach.insert.name: bach.insert
bach.insert.description: Inserts elements at specified addresses of an llll.

inlets.digest: llll to insert the new elements in

outlets.digest: llll with the new elements inserted

bach.integrate.name: bach.integrate
bach.integrate.description: Computes the integral of a breakpoint function or of a general function defined via a lambda loop.

inlets.digest: Breakpoint function llll or sampling parameters

bach.intersection.name: bach.intersection
bach.intersection.description: Returns the intersection of two lllls.

bach.inv.name: bach.inv
bach.inv.digest: Find the inverse of a matrix
bach.inv.description:
Computes the inverse of a square matrix or
		reports when such inverse could not be computed.

outlets.digest: The inverse of the incoming matrix, if any
bang if the incoming matrix is singular
bang if the incoming matrix is not well-shaped or not square

bach.is.name: bach.is
bach.is.description: Returns the type of the incoming data.

inlets.digest: The data whose type will be reported

outlets.digest: The numeric representation of the contained data types
The symbolic representation of the contained data types

bach.istruct.name: bach.istruct
bach.istruct.digest: Get the interval structure pitch-class set
bach.istruct.description:
Reports the interval structure of a pitch-class set, i.e. the list
		of distances between consecutive elements of the (looped) set.

bach.iter.name: bach.iter
bach.iter.description: bach.iter traverses lllls depth-first, outputting their elements one by one.

inlets.digest: bang/stop to stop iteration, or lambda inlet

bach.ivec.name: bach.ivec
bach.ivec.digest: Compute the interval vector of a pitch-class set
bach.ivec.description:
Computes the interval vector of a pitch class-set, i.e. the vector telling
		how many intervals of each kind show up in the set. bach.ivec can also perform multi-interval
		analysis, outputting the multi-interval vector (also known as k-deck).

bach.ker.name: bach.ker
bach.ker.digest: Find the kernel of a matrix
bach.ker.description:
Finds the kernel of an incoming matrix,
		i.e. the set of vectors which are sent to 0 by the matrix multiplication.

bach.keychain.name: bach.keychain
bach.keychain.description:
Classifies the elements of the incoming llll, by associating them with corresponding keys,
		and then by outputting the llll organized by keys.

bach.kurtosis.name: bach.kurtosis
bach.kurtosis.digest: Find the kurtosis of the numbers in an llll
bach.kurtosis.description:
Finds the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of the
		numbers in an llll.

outlets.digest: The kurtosis of all incoming numbers

bach.lace.name: bach.lace
bach.lace.description: Builds an llll by combining the elements of several lllls in a round-robin fashion.

bach.lcm.name: bach.lcm
bach.lcm.description: Computes the least common multiple of two numbers or of an llll.

inlets.digest: The first number or the llll of numbers

outlets.digest: 1 The least common multiple of the numbers

bach.linearsolve.name: bach.linearsolve
bach.linearsolve.digest: Solve a linear system of equations
bach.linearsolve.description:
Solves a linear system of equations in the matrix form Ax = b, where A
		is the system matrix and b is the column vector. If the system is solvable and the solution
		is unique, the vector x is sent through the first outlet. In any case, an information
		about the solvability is sent through the second outlet.

outlets.digest: Number of solutions of the system

bach.llll2dict.name: bach.llll2dict
bach.llll2dict.digest: Convert an llll into a dictionary
bach.llll2dict.description: Converts an llll into a dictionary, under the convention that the first element in each level is the level key.

bach.locate.name: bach.locate
bach.locate.description:
Returns the address of the first occurrence of an element or sequence
		inside an llll

bach.lookup.name: bach.lookup
bach.lookup.digest: Lookup value by key in llll
bach.lookup.description: Lookup value by key in llll

bach.m2jitcellblock.name: bach.m2jitcellblock
bach.m2jitcellblock.digest: Display the content of an llll matrix in a jit.cellblock
bach.m2jitcellblock.description: Shows the content of an llll matrix in the jit.cellblock object.

bach.m2matrixctrl.name: bach.m2matrixctrl
bach.m2matrixctrl.digest: Format an llll matrix to be used with matrixctrl or matrix~
bach.m2matrixctrl.description: Converts an llll matrix in order to pilote a matrix~ or a matrixctrl object.

bach.mapchord.name: bach.mapchord
bach.mapchord.description:
Takes the gathered syntax of a bach.roll or bach.score and operates a given
		transformation on each chord, defined via a lambda loop.

bach.mapelem.name: bach.mapelem
bach.mapelem.description:
Takes an llll and operates a given transformation on each element.
		The transformation is defined via the lambda inlet and outlet.

bach.matrixctrl2m.name: bach.matrixctrl2m
bach.matrixctrl2m.digest: Convert a matrixctrl object into an llll matrix
bach.matrixctrl2m.description:
Converts the information contained in a
		matrixctrl into an llll matrix.

bach.maximum.name: bach.maximum
bach.maximum.description:
Compares every element of the left llll with the corresponding
		element of the right llll, and outputs the bigger.

outlets.digest: The maximum of the two lllls element-wise

bach.mc2n.name: bach.mc2n
bach.mc2n.description: Converts an llll containing midicents into a corresponding llll containing note names.

outlets.digest: The llll containing the note names

bach.mc2p.name: bach.mc2p
bach.mc2p.description: Converts an llll containing cents into a corresponding llll containing pitches.

bach.mc2pc.name: bach.mc2pc
bach.mc2pc.description: Converts an llll containing midicents into an identically structured llll containing the corresponding pitch-classes.

bach.mc2r.name: bach.mc2r
bach.mc2r.description:
Converts an llll containing intervals (expressed in midicents) into an identically structured llll
		containing the corresponding frequency ratios.
		Ratio is reported as a floating point value.

bach.mcapprox.name: bach.mcapprox
bach.mcapprox.description:
Approximates the incoming midicents llll with the nearest pitches in the
		full chromatic range of the chosen microtonal grid.

bach.median.name: bach.median
bach.median.digest: Find the median of the numbers in an llll
bach.median.description: Finds the median of the elements in a flat llll.

outlets.digest: The median of all incoming numbers

bach.minfo.name: bach.minfo
bach.minfo.description:
Outputs the number of rows and columns of an incoming matrix, plus an additional information
		which tells us whether the matrix is well-shaped or square.

outlets.digest: 1 if the matrix is well-shaped, 0 otherwise
1 if the matrix is square, 0 otherwise
1 if the matrix is symmetrical, 0 otherwise

bach.minimum.name: bach.minimum
bach.minimum.description:
Compares every element of the left llll with the corresponding
		element of the right llll, and outputs the smaller.

outlets.digest: The minimum of the two lllls element-wise

bach.minmax.name: bach.minmax
bach.minmax.digest: Min and max of llll elements
bach.minmax.description: Min and max of llll elements

bach.mod.name: bach.mod
bach.mod.description:
Outputs the positive remainders in a division operation
		between lllls or between lllls and numbers.

outlets.digest: The remainder of the division of the two operands

bach.mod*.name: bach.mod*
bach.mod*.description: Performs multiplications modulo a certain integer.

outlets.digest: The modular multiplication of the two operands

bach.mod+.name: bach.mod+
bach.mod+.description: Performs additions modulo a certain integer.

outlets.digest: The modular addition of the two operands

bach.mod-.name: bach.mod-
bach.mod-.description: Performs subtractions modulo a certain integer.

outlets.digest: The modular subtraction of the two operands

bach.mode.name: bach.mode
bach.mode.digest: Find the mode of an llll
bach.mode.description: Finds the number appearing most often in an llll.

bach.mono.name: bach.mono
bach.mono.description:
Turns a generic bach.roll (possibly containing overlapping notes)
		into a monophonic one, by trimming the note tails if needed.

inlets.digest: The llll containing the gathered syntax of the original
Voices to be made monophonic (list of 0's and 1's)

outlets.digest: The llll containing the gathered syntax of the monophonic

bach.mpow.name: bach.mpow
bach.mpow.digest: Compute the power of a matrix
bach.mpow.description: Raises the incoming square matrix to a given integer power.

outlets.digest: The power of the incoming matrix

bach.pcsetinfo.name: bach.pcsetinfo
bach.pcsetinfo.digest: Report basic information about a pitch-class set
bach.pcsetinfo.description:
Reports some standard information about a pitch-class set, such as its
		cardinality, whether it is in prime form (or not), whether it is symmetrical (or not), its interval
		structure period, and its periodicity (number of different transpositions).   
		In the standard framework, the modulo is the number of subdivision of the octave (represented as a circle). The modulo is thus the number of
		points in this circle. The default and most common modulo is 12 (corresponding to semitonal grid). Modulo 24 is the quartertone grid, and so on.
		 
		A pitch-class set is a plain collection of pitch-classes. A pitch class is nothing but the representative of a set of pitches.
		Traditionally, it corresponds to the concept of "note", once we abstract it from its octave.
		For instance, the semitonal framework (when the modulo is 12), all the C belong to the same pitch-class
		which will be named 0 = {..., C-1, C0, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, ...}. The pitch-class 1 will be the one containing all C#'s (or Db's); pitch-class
		2 will contain all D's, and so on. One will use to name pitch class numbers from 0 to the modulo - 1: indeed, with modulo = 12, pitch-class 12 will coincide
		with pitch-class 0 (it'll be the C one octave higher). One can thus think at pitch-classes as equally spaced points on a clock, and transposing
		means rotating them on the clock. A pitch class set is thus represented just by a plain list of pitch classes, such 0 4 7, representing the
		C major chord. Notice that this coincides with any other representation such as 12 4 19 or 0 -8 -5, but the canonical form, where numbers
		are from 0 to the modulo-1 is always preferred. Also for pitch-class sets the order of elements is immaterial, and thus
		0 4 7 or 4 0 7 or 7 4 0 will all represent the same set.
		On the other hand a pitch-class (as an abstract concept) can be used to represent things other than pitches,
		as for instance temporal position in a rhythmic pattern (loop) having a certain number (the modulo) of equally spaced elements.

outlets.digest: Is in prime form (with respect to transpositions?)
Is in prime form (with respect to transpositions/inversion?)
